\[
c(x) = \arg\min_j \lVert x - \mu_j \rVert^2,
\quad
\mu_j = \frac{1}{|C_j|} \sum_{x \in C_j} x,
\qquad k = 4
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(x\): The color of a pixel
- \(\mu_j\): The center of cluster j
- \(C_j\): The colors in cluster j
- \(c(x)\): The cluster of color x

x is the color of a pixel and mu_j the center of cluster j. Lloyd's algorithm repeats two steps. It assigns each color to its nearest center, and it moves each center to the mean of its colors. Both steps lower the sum of squared distances or keep it, so the steps settle. PixelNexus runs them on the distinct colors weighted by how often they appear, which gives the same means as running on every pixel. The result depends on the start, and k-means usually starts at random. PixelNexus uses its own deterministic start, so the same image always gives the same clusters. The first center is the color nearest to the mean color. Each next one is the color farthest from the centers so far. Ties go to the smaller color code 65536 R + 256 G + B. A cluster that loses all its colors keeps its center. An image with fewer distinct colors than k gets fewer clusters.
